title: Pampangga sugarcane (Phil 75 44): Characteristics
metaDescription: Pampangga sugarcane is an older public clone sugarcane variety. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Pampangga sugarcane is an older public clone sugarcane variety, also sold or known as Phil 75 44 or Pampanga cane. It is not on the NSIC registry, so the facts here come from its seller and farm sources.

heroImage.alt: Cane setts laid in deep furrows on red soil, the start of a sugarcane crop, the kind of farm where Pampangga sugarcane is grown

blocks.text: If you came here looking for Phil 75 44 or Pampanga cane, this is the same sugarcane. The facts below come from its seller and from farm sources, each one listed at the end. Compare it with the others in our [sugarcane variety finder](/crop-varieties/sugarcane), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for sugarcane](/land-preparation/sugarcane-land-preparation).

blocks.caption: From its seller and farm sources

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

The registry gives no day count or trial yield for this variety. So ask the seller or your municipal agriculturist for figures from farms near you before you plan a season around it.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
The registry gives no pest or disease ratings for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit sugarcane fields most often: [Rice field rats](/pests/rice-field-rats), [Corn downy mildew](/diseases/corn-downy-mildew), [white grub](/pests/white-grub). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
What its seller and farm sources say

Why farmers know it: covered nearly 70 percent of cane fields in the Don Pedro (Nasugbu, Batangas) mill district in 2003, planters there stuck with it because neighbors grew it. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant Pampangga sugarcane

Mills pay for sugar, not cane, so compare the sugar yield in LKg per hectare as well as the tonnes of cane. Pick a variety that ratoons well, and one rated against smut and downy mildew, the diseases that cut a ratoon crop short. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Land preparation in the Philippines](/land-preparation/land-preparation-philippines).

items: Buy sealed packs or tagged sacks from an accredited dealer, and check the packing date and germination rate.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Try it on a small area first, beside the variety you usually plant, before you switch the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is Phil 75 44 the same as Pampangga?
items.a: Yes. Phil 75 44 is another name for Pampangga. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Pampangga?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
